headline: At least 24 dead and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian candy factory
standfirst: A major fire at a confectionery manufacturing facility in western Java has left at least 24 workers dead and around 30 missing.
keyPoints: A massive fire struck a confectionery plant in Banten province, killing at least 24 people.
Roughly 30 workers remain missing as search teams navigate unstable ruins.
Police report severe burn injuries will require DNA testing to identify victims.
A faulty air conditioning unit is suspected as a possible cause of the blaze.

paragraphs: Emergency crews in western Indonesia have recovered at least 24 bodies following a massive blaze at a confectionery manufacturing plant. The inferno began during the late afternoon on Saturday in Banten province, located on the island of Java. Dozens of workers were caught inside the facility as flames rapidly spread through the structure. Firefighters worked through the night before successfully putting out the blaze early the next morning.

The incident occurred in the Cikande district within the Serang Regency, approximately one hour from the capital city of Jakarta. Search and rescue operations were immediately launched to locate missing personnel who remained unaccounted for after the fire. Rescuers faced hazardous conditions while navigating the collapsed framework and charred debris of the industrial site. Local authorities confirmed that a significant number of employees were present when the fire first erupted.

Disaster response personnel continue to comb through the destroyed building in search of additional victims. Authorities report that roughly 30 employees remain missing following the weekend catastrophe. Images recorded at the scene showed extensive structural damage, including caved-in roof sections and incinerated vehicles outside. The facility operated as a key production hub for a prominent domestic sweet manufacturer.

sections.heading: Industrial context and site details
paragraphs: The affected property belonged to Fonusa Agung Mulia, a confectionery enterprise operating in western Java. The business functions as a subsidiary under UNIFAM, a major food manufacturing group based in Indonesia. Operations at the facility focused primarily on producing various sweet goods for domestic and regional distribution. Hundreds of local residents rely on the industrial area in Banten province for employment opportunities.

Industrial estates near Jakarta have grown rapidly over recent decades to support the country's expanding food processing sector. Facilities in Serang Regency house multiple manufacturing plants that process agricultural products and commercial goods. The sudden disaster has raised questions regarding safety protocols and emergency preparedness within major industrial zones across Java. Authorities are reviewing operational records for the site as part of their preliminary assessment.

sections.heading: Official statements and cause investigation
paragraphs: Official investigations into the origin of the fatal incident are currently underway led by regional authorities. A presidential adviser on workers' welfare, Said Iqbal, indicated that an electrical fault within the air conditioning network might have triggered the disaster. However, officials emphasized that comprehensive technical examinations must be completed before an official conclusion is reached. Forensic experts are working alongside emergency responders to inspect the damaged electrical infrastructure.

Identifying the recovered remains has presented severe challenges for forensic teams working on site. Regional police chief inspector general Hendra Kurniawan explained that the victims "were no longer physically identifiable" due to the extreme heat. Consequently, medical specialists will rely on detailed DNA comparisons to confirm the identities of those who perished. Family members of missing workers have been requested to assist authorities by providing genetic samples.

sections.heading: Search efforts and worker safety impact
paragraphs: Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency, known locally as Basarnas, has deployed specialist teams to examine the ruins. Rescuers are carefully moving through unstable building components to prevent further collapses during the search effort. Video released by the agency depicted emergency personnel shifting heavy debris to access isolated sections of the factory floor. Heavy machinery and specialized search tools are being utilized to reach submerged or buried areas.

The tragedy has renewed attention on workplace protection standards for factory laborers across the Southeast Asian nation. Labor representatives have voiced deep concern regarding emergency evacuation routes and safety systems in large manufacturing plants. Public officials are facing calls to conduct thorough safety inspections of similar industrial facilities operating in the surrounding region. Preventing similar industrial disasters remains a priority for regional government authorities.

sections.heading: Ongoing inquiries and next steps
paragraphs: Recovery personnel plan to remain at the Cikande site until all missing workers are fully accounted for. Search teams are prioritizing structural stabilization so that forensic teams can safely conduct detailed examinations of the entire footprint. Local administrators are providing support services to affected families waiting for news regarding missing relatives. Authorities expect the search operation to continue over the coming days.

Government investigators will compile a comprehensive report detailing the safety breaches or technical failures that contributed to the blaze. Legal and regulatory reviews may follow once the exact cause of the electrical fault or fire ignition is formally established. The corporate parent company is expected to cooperate fully with public investigators assessing safety compliance at the facility. Further official updates regarding victim identification will be released as DNA testing results become available.

timeline.what: A fire breaks out at the Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Banten province around 4:30 pm local time.
Emergency crews extinguish the fire by 6:30 am and police announce DNA testing will be needed for victim identification.
Officials confirm 24 fatalities and launch a welfare inquiry as search teams seek about 30 missing employees.

socialSummary: At least 24 people have died and dozens remain missing after a massive fire destroyed a candy factory in western Java.
